prompts: We need a landing page, {WS}/landing/index.html in a single file, for the story of Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
**[goal]** Build a single-file landing page, `landing/index.html`, about Mondrian's *Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow* (1930), using only what FACTSHEET.md says.

**[action]**
- Built the page from plain CSS grids. The black gaps between cells act as the thick black lines on a white ground.
- The opening section is laid out like the picture the fact sheet describes: a large red block at top right, a small blue one at bottom left and a small yellow one at bottom right.
- The second section covers the painter, the year, the medium, the collection, De Stijl, Neoplasticism and why the work matters. The page's colours are limited to the ones the fact sheet names: red, blue, yellow, white, grey and black.
- A yellow call-to-action block links to the Wikipedia source the fact sheet gives.
- Assumptions:
  - I left out three.js. A flat 2D page fits the "only horizontal and vertical lines" rule better.
  - The Archivo font loads from Google Fonts, with Arial as the fallback.
  - On narrow screens the grid collapses to one column.
  - The page carries a note that the layout is a tribute in CSS, not a copy of the painting.

**[result]**
- Every claim on the page comes from a fact sheet line, and none goes beyond it. I checked this by comparing the text to FACTSHEET.md, not with a tool.
- The link points to `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composition_with_Red,_Blue_and_Yellow`, the same URL as the fact sheet.
- The page has no scripts and needs no build step. The only outside request is Google Fonts, which the review browser can reach.
- **Not verified:** I didn't open the page in a browser or take a screenshot, so the layout and the mobile switch-over are untested. My only check was the edit output, which shows the mobile rule in place: `.cta,.foot{grid-column:1;grid-row:auto}`.

**[next]** Open the file in a browser at full width and at about 375 px to confirm the layout.
